findings.source: CJEU case law — InfoCuria (curia.europa.eu/juris, infocuria.curia.europa.eu) + EUR-Lex + Publications Office Cellar

access.auth: none — public, no key. Send headers: Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, Accept: application/json, Origin: https://infocuria.curia.europa.eu, Referer: https://infocuria.curia.europa.eu/ (all working scrapers send Origin; two also send Referer)
access.detail:
RECOMMENDED PRIMARY FOR SEARCH. JSON backend of the NEW InfoCuria SPA (infocuria.curia.europa.eu, the court's own live index since its ~June 2025 relaunch; includes same-day and unpublished decisions). Endpoints (verbatim from 5 independent codebases incl. two MCP servers):

1) SEARCH: POST /elastic-connector/search — JSON body (verbatim, ahjucaf/juricaf + davzavada/IP-rss-feed + metaneutrons/german-legal-mcp):
{"searchTerm":"","multiSearchTerms":[],"sortTermList":[{"sortDirection":"DESC","sortTerm":"SCORE"}],"pagination":{"pageNumber":0,"pageSize":20,"from":1,"to":20},"language":"EN","tabName":"affair","isAllTabsRequest":false,"ecli":"","publishedId":"","usualName":"","logicDocId":"","repJurExpand":true,"filtersValue":[],"advancedFiltersValue":[],"isSearchExact":true,"searchSources":["document","metadata"]}
Field semantics: searchTerm = full-text keywords (searchSources ["document","metadata"] = document text + metadata); publishedId = case number, e.g. "C-691/26" (put the quoted case number in searchTerm too for exact match); ecli = ECLI:EU:C:...; usualName = case usual name/parties; sortTerm: "SCORE" | "INTRODUCTION_DATE"; tabName: "affair" | "jurisprudence" | "tout_jurisprudence"; filtersValue entries e.g. {"field":"affairState","values":["CLOTPUB"],"valuesWithFullHierarchy":["CLOTPUB"]} (closed+published), {"field":"jurisdiction","values":["C"]} (C=Court of Justice, T=General Court); advancedFiltersValue entries e.g. {"field":"typeDoc","values":["OBSRP_PUB"],"valuesWithFullHierarchy":[],"isMatchAll":false}; pageSize up to 1000 observed working. GET form also seen seeded as /elastic-connector/search?page=0&size=20&lang=EN.
Response: {totalHits, searchHits:[{...affId..., innerHits:{document:{searchHits:[{document/content: {docTypeCode, docDate, docLang, docFormats, logicDocId, docNoPart, groupByLogicalId, idProcedure, parties, matCode/matCodeML, advocateML, avg, reportingJudge/reportingJudgeML, procedureResultTypeML, affObjectML, contentML, author, authorCode, joinAffairs, pourvoiAffIds, originPourvoiIds, ...}}]}}}]}

2) SUGGEST (case-number → affair id): POST /elastic-connector/suggest — {"searchTerm":"C-73/24","language":"EN","tabName":"jurisprudence"} → in response list match procedureDocInfo.idPublished == case number, take procedureDocInfo.id as affId.

3) CASE FILE: POST /elastic-connector/affairId/procedures — {"affId":<id>,"searchTerm":"C-73/24","tabName":"jurisprudence","language":"EN"} → documents at searchHits[0].innerHits.document.searchHits.

4) DOCUMENT TEXT: GET /blob/download-file/{logicDocId}/{LANG}/html (strip "id_" prefix from logicDocId; also .../{LANG}/PDF). Alternative long form (maastrichtlawtech/cellar-extractor): GET /blob/download-file-html/{jurisdiction}/{year}/{process}/{logicDocId}-{doclang}-1.html where idProcedure like "C/24/0073" gives jurisdiction=split('/')[0], year=split('/')[2], process=idProcedure.replace('/','_'). PDFs also served from https://infocuria.curia.europa.eu/document/{jur}-...-{logicDocId}-{part}-{LANG}.pdf. Case page URL: https://infocuria.curia.europa.eu/tabs/affair?...  No auth on any of these; standard fetch works (no JS, no cookies).

RECOMMENDED PRIMARY FOR TEXT RETRIEVAL (Cellar REST, official Publications Office dissemination API). GET /resource/celex/{CELEX} (CJEU case law is CELEX sector 6: 6 + year + type + 4-digit number; C-311/18 judgment = 62018CJ0311; type letters: CJ judgment, CO order, CC AG opinion; General Court TJ/TO) with headers Accept: application/xhtml+xml, text/html (CJEU judgments are served as text/html — try xhtml first then html; verbatim from cyanheads/eur-lex-mcp-server) and Accept-Language: 3-letter ISO 639-2/T code (eng, deu, fra — bibliographic ger/fre are rejected); follow redirects. If requested language has no content → retry with eng. HTTP 300 = multi-part document: body lists sibling part URLs to fetch and concatenate. ECLI-BASED RETRIEVAL: GET /resource/ecli/ECLI:EU:C:2020:559 dereferences the same work (EUR-Lex's own judgment HTML hyperlinks cites as http://publications.europa.eu/resource/ecli/ECLI%3AEU%3AC%3A2016%3A514 including #point{n} paragraph anchors — quoted verbatim from EUR-Lex-derived corpora on GitHub). Metadata notices per official Cellar docs: Accept: application/xml;notice=object | notice=tree | notice=branch; RDF via Accept: application/rdf+xml. Used by production code as the WAF-free fallback when eur-lex.europa.eu blocks bots.

Cellar SPARQL (Virtuoso) — best route for structured criteria search by ECLI/CELEX/date and for the citation graph. GET with ?query={urlencoded}&format=application%2Fsparql-results%2Bjson, or POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded with fields query and format=application/sparql-results+json; header Accept: application/sparql-results+json (or +xml). PREFIX cdm: <http://publications.europa.eu/ontology/cdm#>. Case-law CDM properties (verbatim from 6 codebases): ?work cdm:case-law_ecli ?ecli ; cdm:resource_legal_id_celex ?celex ; cdm:work_date_document ?date ; cdm:work_has_resource-type ?type (URIs: http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/JUDG | ORDER | OPIN_AG) ; cdm:case-law_delivered_by_court-formation ?formation ; citations via cdm:work_cites_work. Titles/parties: ?expr cdm:expression_belongs_to_work ?work ; cdm:expression_uses_language <http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/language/ENG> ; cdm:expression_title ?title. Filter CJEU docs with FILTER(REGEX(?celex,'^6[0-9]{4}CJ')) or court patterns CJ|CO|CC (CJEU) vs TJ|TO (GC); dates with FILTER(?date >= "2024-01-01"^^xsd:date); keyword search on titles with Virtuoso bif:contains. Paginate with ORDER BY DESC(?date) LIMIT n OFFSET m. Quirks (verbatim from cyanheads/eur-lex-mcp-server): Virtuoso returns HTTP 200 with error text in body — detect /Virtuoso\s+\d+\s+Error/ and /SP031|query execution timed out/; when rate-limited it returns an HTML page instead of SPARQL results; ~100s server-side timeout; dedupe results by ECLI (spurious _RES variants).

CLASSIC InfoCuria JSF GET interface — still live (working scrapes in GitHub code through Nov 2025) and works with plain fetch (requests/scrapy, no JS, no cookies; cid= is an optional session id, any value or omitted). Working combos quoted verbatim from scrapers:
- All documents of a case: GET /documents.jsf?num=C-561/19 (num accepts C-…/…, T-…/…).
- Case list: GET /liste.jsf?language=en&jur=C,T,F&num=C-283/81 (jur: C=Court of Justice, T=General Court, F=CST).
- Criteria listing with pagination (lest161c/cjeu-ali, plain requests.get over 776 pages): GET /documents.jsf?nat=or&mat=or&pcs=Oor&jur=C%2CT&num=C-&for=&jge=&dates=&language=en&pro=&cit=none%252CC%252CCJ%252CR%252C2008E%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252C%252Ctrue%252Cfalse%252Cfalse&oqp=&td=%3B%3B%3BPUB1%3BNPUB1%3B%3B%3BORDALL&avg=&lgrec=en&page={n}&lg=  — td selects document types (';ALL' = everything; PUB1 = judgments published in ECR; NPUB1 = unpublished judgments; ORDALL suffix); date windows encode as td=$mode=fromTo$from=1952.01.01$to=2018.12.31;;NPUB;PUB1,PUB2,PUB7;NPUB1,NPUB2,NPUB3;;;ORDALL or $mode=1M (last month); etat=clot filters closed cases; parse CELEX ids off the page with regex r'CELEX:(.*?)[\'"]'.
- Document text: GET /document/document.jsf?text=&docid={internal_numeric_id}&pageIndex=0&doclang=EN&mode=lst&dir=&occ=first&part=1&cid=1 (mode=DOC|lst|req all seen working; docid comes from the list page links).
- CELEX shortcut (no docid needed): GET /celex.jsf?celex=62012CJ0131&lang1=en&type=TXT&ancre= — resolves a CELEX straight to the document view.
NOT ESTABLISHED: a pure-GET full-text keyword parameter for the classic interface (the search form recherche.jsf posts JSF state); use the elastic-connector searchTerm for full text instead.

EUR-Lex website — usable for retrieval by CELEX but NOT recommended from serverless: GET /legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62012CJ0293 (page), /legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:{celex} (bare HTML), /legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:... (metadata). GET search: /search.html?scope=EURLEX&text={query}&lang=en&type=quick&page={n} plus subdomain filters like DTS_SUBDOM=... (case-law subdomain EU_CASE_LAW; qid is an auto-added session-ish number). CAVEAT (verbatim from openlegaldata/oldp-ingestor): the site sits behind an AWS WAF — bot fetches intermittently get an aws-waf-token challenge; production ingestors detect it and fall back to https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/{celex}. Some pages carry an <?xml encoding=...?> prolog that breaks lxml.html parsing.

access.auth: registration — free but gated: EU Login account + web-service access request via My EUR-Lex, approved by an administrator; credentials sent per request in a WS-Security UsernameToken SOAP header
access.detail: SOAP (not REST) search web service. WSDL: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EURLexWebService?wsdl. Accepts expert-search query language (same criteria as website expert search, incl. CELEX sector 6 case law: DTS_SUBDOM=EU_CASE_LAW style criteria), returns XML notices — metadata only, not full text (fetch text separately via Cellar/EUR-Lex by CELEX). Docs: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/help/data-reuse/webservice.html and the Web Service User Manual PDF (eur-lex.europa.eu/content/tools/webservices/SearchWebServiceUserManual_v2.00.pdf). NOT recommended for a serverless Node MCP: registration friction, SOAP envelope construction, XML parsing, and CJEU coverage/freshness is inferior to InfoCuria (EUR-Lex itself notes decisions delivered after 20 June 2025 are temporarily not retrievable by subject matter, directing users to CURIA).

findings.caveats: RECOMMENDATION for a serverless (Vercel, Node fetch, stateless) MCP: (1) SEARCH via POST https://infocuriaws.curia.europa.eu/elastic-connector/search — the new InfoCuria's own JSON API: one endpoint covers case number (publishedId), ECLI, parties/usual name (usualName), full-text keywords (searchTerm with searchSources ["document","metadata"]), court/state/doc-type filters, sorting and pagination, and is the freshest source (same-day judgments, unpublished decisions). (2) TEXT via GET https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/{CELEX} (or /resource/ecli/{ECLI}) with Accept: application/xhtml+xml, text/html and 3-letter Accept-Language — stable, WAF-free, no auth; for documents too new for Cellar, fall back to InfoCuria GET /blob/download-file/{logicDocId}/{LANG}/html. (3) Use Cellar SPARQL for structured metadata (ECLI↔CELEX resolution, date-range lists, citation graph). Caveats: the elastic-connector API is UNDOCUMENTED and unofficial (cellar-extractor: "undocumented; observed live") — it already replaced the old juris backend once (June 2025), so pin nothing and keep the classic curia.europa.eu/juris GET interface (still live) as a fallback; send Origin/Referer headers mimicking the SPA. No published rate limits anywhere; production scrapers pace ~0.05s/request to infocuriaws and use modest page sizes (20–100; 1000 observed working); Cellar SPARQL throttles under load by returning an HTML page (detect non-JSON body) and Virtuoso errors arrive as HTTP 200 bodies (match /Virtuoso \d+ Error/, SP031 = timeout). Avoid eur-lex.europa.eu HTML from datacenter IPs (AWS WAF bot challenges). Mapping pitfalls: one case has many documents (judgment CJ, order CO, AG opinion CC) and joined cases share texts — ECLI is the safest per-document key; derive CELEX from case number as 6+year+type+zero-padded number (C-131/12 judgment → 62012CJ0131) but verify via SPARQL since the year in CELEX is the case year, and non-EN texts may be the only ones available for older/unpublished decisions (some texts exist only in French/language of the case — then only on InfoCuria). EUR-Lex/Cellar covers published CJEU case law comprehensively (sector 6) but lags InfoCuria for the newest decisions, and subject-matter search for post-20-June-2025 decisions is temporarily broken on EUR-Lex per its own notice. Licensing: EU law texts are reusable (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU); curia.europa.eu legal notice permits reuse with source acknowledgment; CJEU texts note that only versions in the Reports/OJ are authentic. Could NOT establish: any official documentation for the elastic-connector API (none exists publicly), a pure-GET full-text parameter for the classic juris interface, and infocuriaws behavior under sustained datacenter-IP load (no WAF reports found, and at least one Vercel-style cron scraper — davzavada/IP-rss-feed — uses it successfully, but this is inference, not proof).

findings.source: EUIPO eSearch Case Law (https://euipo.europa.eu/eSearchCLW/) — EUIPO BoA/Opposition/Cancellation/Examination decisions + GC/CJEU and national-court IP judgments

access.auth: none — no API key, no OAuth; plain POST works server-side (verbatim from a scraper that successfully fetched samples on 2026-03-20). Send browser-like User-Agent, Accept: application/json, Content-Type: application/json.
access.detail: eSearchCLW IS a SPA with an undocumented JSON backend under /caselaw/. SEARCH (confirmed verbatim in working code, worldwidelaw/legal-sources bootstrap.py + config.yaml): POST https://euipo.europa.eu/caselaw/officesearch/json/{lang} (lang e.g. 'en') for the Trade mark decisions tab (BoA appeals, oppositions, cancellations, examinations; ~342,000+ records); POST https://euipo.europa.eu/caselaw/rcdsearch/json/{lang} for the Design decisions tab. Endpoints for the National Court judgments and Preliminary rulings tabs were NOT established (likely sibling paths under /caselaw/, unverified). POST body (verbatim, works): {"resultsPerPage": 50, "start": 0, "criteria": [], "sort": {"field": "DecisionDate", "order": "desc"}}. Pagination: offset in 'start' + 'resultsPerPage'; response 'numFound' gives total; loop start += len(results). RESPONSE shape (field names verbatim): top-level {numFound, results[], errorLabel (set on error)}; each result: uniqueSolrKey, caseNumber, type/typeLabel (OPPOSITION|CANCELLATION|EXAMINATION|APPEAL), ipRight ('EUTM', 'RCD', 'IR designating the EU'), entityName (trade mark name; '(Trade mark without text)' for figurative), entityNumber, entityType (e.g. 'Figurative'), date (DD/MM/YYYY), outcome (e.g. 'Reject opposition: opposition not admissible'), norms[] (e.g. 'Article 8(1)(b) EUTMR'), appealed ('Yes'/'No'), url, languagesOriginal[] = [{code: 'en', pdfUrl: ...}]. uniqueSolrKey format: {TYPE}_{YYYYMMDD}_{caseOrOppositionNo}_{entityNumber}, e.g. OPP_20260319_003250868_W01861857; observed prefixes OPP, CCL, RFS, APL. UNRESOLVED: the element shape of a non-empty 'criteria' array (how keyword/caseNumber/date-range/trademark-name filters are encoded as JSON) — no public code performs a filtered search; only sort field 'DecisionDate' is confirmed, suggesting PascalCase Solr-style field names. The UI's advanced search exposes filters for keywords, legal norms, case number, trade mark name, decision date range, decision type, BoA rapporteur, document type (GC/CJ), court name (national) — one DevTools capture in a browser would pin the JSON encoding. Deep links (verbatim from published links): decision view https://euipo.europa.eu/eSearchCLW/#key/trademark/{uniqueSolrKey}; basic search by case number https://euipo.europa.eu/eSearchCLW/#basic/*///number/{caseNumber URL-encoded, e.g. 176%2F2004-2}.

access.auth: none, but session cookies required: GET https://euipo.europa.eu/eSearchCLW/ first to establish cookies, then send Referer: https://euipo.europa.eu/eSearchCLW/ and Accept: */* on the download request (verbatim from working scraper).
access.detail: DOCUMENT RETRIEVAL: the languagesOriginal[].pdfUrl values point at the 'copla' backend. Verbatim URL pattern observed in published links: https://euipo.europa.eu/copla/trademark/data/{applicationNumber}/download/CLW/{DOCTYPE}/{YYYY}/{LANG}/{YYYYMMDD}_{casenum}.pdf?app=caselaw&casenum={casenum}&trTypeDoc=NA — real examples: .../013682299/download/CLW/APL/2017/EN/20170622_R1933_2016-4.pdf?app=caselaw&casenum=R1933/2016-4&trTypeDoc=NA (BoA decision R 1933/2016-4); .../008320591/download/CLW/ECJ/2019/EN/20190411_T-655_17.pdf?app=caselaw&casenum=T-655/17&trTypeDoc=NA (GC judgment T-655/17); .../010392835/download/CLW/CCL/2019/EN/20190731_000014787.doc?app=caselaw&casenum=000014787&trTypeDoc=NA (cancellation 14787C). DOCTYPE codes seen: APL (appeal/BoA), ECJ (GC/CJEU), CCL (cancellation); files are PDF or .doc (the .doc files are actually DOCX). Adjacent same-platform endpoints (eSearch plus, for context): POST https://euipo.europa.eu/copla/ctmsearch/json with form-encoded body start=0&rows=100&searchMode=basic&criterion_1=ApplicationNumber&term_1=...&operator_1=OR&condition_1=CONTAINS&sortField=ApplicationNumber&sortOrder=asc, and GET https://euipo.europa.eu/copla/trademark/data/withOppoRelations/{applicationNumber} returning JSON {items[], total} / {entity:{...}} — shows the copla platform's criterion/term/operator/condition query DSL and PascalCase field names (ApplicationNumber, MarkVerbalElementText, OppositionIdentifier), which the caselaw 'criteria' array probably mirrors in JSON form (inference, not confirmed).

access.auth: OAuth 2.0 client_credentials (scope 'uid'). Token URL: https://auth.euipo.europa.eu/oidc/accessToken (POST grant_type=client_credentials + client_id + client_secret + scope=uid). Every request must carry BOTH 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' AND 'X-IBM-Client-Id: <client_id>'. Register an App at https://dev.euipo.europa.eu (production) or https://dev-sandbox.euipo.europa.eu (sandbox, separate auth realm; base https://api-sandbox.euipo.europa.eu); subscribe to products on the Default Plan. Sandbox activates instantly; PRODUCTION requires sending identity documents to docs.apiplatform@euipo.europa.eu (passport for natural persons, company register excerpt for legal persons). Default Plan: 25,000 calls/day per app; token lifetime 7,200 s; HTTP 429 on overage.
access.detail: OFFICIAL EUIPO developer portal (dev.euipo.europa.eu) — the sanctioned API. CRITICAL FINDING: its product catalogue covers ONLY register data — Trademark Search v1 (GET /trademark-search/trademarks with RSQL 'query' param, e.g. wordMarkSpecification.verbalElement==*Apple* and status==REGISTERED; GET /trademarks/{applicationNumber}; /image, /image/thumbnail, /sound, /video, /model sub-resources; page size 10-100), Design Search v1 (GET /design-search/designs RSQL; /designs/{designNumber}; /views/{order}), Design Filing, image search. There is NO product for case law / Boards of Appeal decisions — confirmed by a 2025-era third-party survey ('No documented public REST API' for eSearchCLW; the 2024/2025 'Enhancements to eSearch Case Law' announcements are UI-only) and by the portal product lists quoted in multiple client repos. The Open Data Platform (https://euipo.europa.eu/ohimportal/en/open-data, free registration, daily XML dumps) likewise covers only the EUTM/RCD register, not decisions. Trademark records do carry a 'decisionDate' field for opposition outcomes, but not decision texts. For the GC/CJEU layer indexed in eSearchCLW, the sanctioned alternative is EUR-Lex/CELLAR (SPARQL + REST, no auth) and curia.europa.eu.

findings.caveats: (1) UNOFFICIAL, UNDOCUMENTED, NO CONTRACT: the /caselaw/officesearch/json endpoint is the SPA's internal XHR; a third-party survey explicitly rates it 'undocumented and unstable... feasible to scrape but not contract-stable'. EUIPO shipped UI enhancements to eSearchCLW in Dec 2024/2025 and the endpoint may change without notice. (2) Could NOT verify live from this environment (euipo.europa.eu, wipo.int, web.archive.org all egress-blocked); however the worldwidelaw scraper's committed sample files carry _fetched_at 2026-03-20 timestamps, proving the endpoint worked with plain server-side requests (Python requests, no browser) five months ago. (3) The non-empty 'criteria' JSON shape is the one unestablished piece — filtered search (keywords/case number/date/trademark name) needs a one-time browser DevTools capture; empty-criteria + date-sorted pagination is fully proven. (4) Bot protection risk: a 2019 scraper of the sibling copla/ctmsearch endpoint resorted to a rotating-proxy service 'to bypass bot detection'; the 2026 caselaw scraper needed only a browser User-Agent for search, but PDF/DOC downloads require prior session cookies (GET /eSearchCLW/) plus a Referer header — statefulness a serverless function must replay per invocation (do the cookie GET and download in the same invocation). Vercel datacenter IPs may still trip a WAF — untested. (5) Scraper self-imposed rate limit: 0.5 req/s with 2 s delays; respect it. (6) Response dates are DD/MM/YYYY; some 'pdf' documents are actually DOCX served as .doc. (7) National Court judgments and Preliminary rulings tab endpoints not established. (8) Licensing: EUIPO decisions are public documents, reuse authorised with attribution per EUIPO legal notice; the official API's production tier is gated on identity-document review and its ToU. (9) Official API path exists ONLY for register data (trademarks/designs), not case law — an MCP server needing BoA decisions must use the unofficial JSON backend or nothing.

findings.source: ÚPV (Czech Industrial Property Office) — ISDV "Databáze správních a soudních rozhodnutí" (isdv.upv.gov.cz/webapp/dbr.rozhodnuti.Prochazet)

access.auth: none (no login, no session cookie required; state travels as ID tokens in URLs)
access.detail: THE DECISIONS DATABASE ITSELF. The ISDV /webapp/ path is an Oracle PL/SQL-gateway-style app (mod_plsql pattern): URLs are package.procedure names, resolved CASE-INSENSITIVELY (dbr.rozhodnuti.Prochazet == dbr.rozhodnuti.prochazet), parameters are plain query-string/form fields matching PL/SQL argument names, pages are fully server-rendered HTML (no JS-required SPA). Two lines exist: (1) SPRÁVNÍ LINIE (administrative decisions of the ÚPV president since 1999 + follow-on Czech court and ECJ/CFI decisions): entry/browse = GET /webapp/rozhodnuti.prochazet (verbatim, Google-indexed; page title 'Databáze správních a soudních rozhodnutí (správní linie)'); alias GET /webapp/dbr.rozhodnuti.Prochazet (verbatim in WIPO PAPI survey response CZ, as https://isdv.upv.cz/webapp/dbr.rozhodnuti.prochazet). Browse is a two-level category tree (level 1: patenty, ochranné známky, užitné vzory, průmyslové vzory, dodatková ochranná osvědčení, označení původu/zeměpisná označení, ostatní; level 2 e.g. for patents: zastavení řízení, zamítnutí přihlášky, zrušení patentu, určení, ostatní rozhodnutí, rozhodnutí ESD — per Ikaros review). Results list = /webapp/rozhodnuti.SeznamRozhodnuti (verbatim, Google-indexed WITHOUT query string — the search form very likely POSTs to it; exact field names NOT established from outside). A 'Vyhledat' (search) mode exists alongside 'Procházet'; fulltext supports AND/OR operators and % wildcard, diacritics-sensitive (per Ikaros). DECISION TEXT: GET /webapp/rozhodnuti.showDocP?p_id={8-char alphanumeric opaque token}, e.g. p_id=LXDatkyH, p_id=qPhlsaTY, p_id=TisUZLXz, p_id=AdyhJoUA — returns server-rendered HTML titled 'Databáze rozhodnutí - náhled' containing the FULL anonymized decision text (Google snippets show decision bodies, e.g. sp. zn. O 131254, decision of 9. 8. 2001). p_id tokens are only obtainable from the list pages (no algorithmic construction found); no PDF sibling endpoint found. (2) SOUDNÍ LINIE (civil-line court judgments, e.g. Městský soud v Praze): GET /webapp/dbr.rozsudek.seznam (verbatim; title 'Databáze soudních rozhodnutí'); its per-judgment detail procedure was not established. Serverless-friendly: no cookies observed in any documented flow; a cookie-consent banner exists but content is served regardless. For an MCP server: fetch rozhodnuti.prochazet / SeznamRozhodnuti, parse HTML (cheerio), follow showDocP links; MUST first fetch the live form HTML once (from an unblocked environment) to read the form's method/action and input names — that is the one thing this research could not verify because isdv.upv.gov.cz, upv.gov.cz, web.archive.org and Common Crawl were all egress-blocked here.

PROVEN QUERY-ENGINE FLOW OF THE SAME ISDV WEBAPP (resdb = rešeršní databáze for patents/TM/designs) — verbatim from working Python scraper github.com/bejka2012/Patenty_BI — the decisions app is built on the same framework and the flow is the best available blueprint: STEP 1 GET /webapp/resdb.dotaz.getDotazID → response body = plain-text query token (format like 'RES0000000032737595ctFSDVuH'). STEP 2 POST /webapp/!resdb.formxml.make (note the '!' mod_plsql flexible-parameter prefix) with form fields: idform=PT, formtyp=A, iddotaz={token}, iduser=-1, lan=CS, plus criteria encoded as XPath-ish field names: 'dotaz/polozka[2]/@co'='CIPV', 'dotaz/polozka[2]/@jak'='=', 'dotaz/polozka[2]/hodnota'={application number}, 'dotaz/polozka[9]/@co'='SKUP', 'dotaz/polozka[9]/hodnota'={type}. STEP 3 POST /webapp/resdb.hitlist.isEmpty?pFrmId=PT&pD={Date.now() ms} → body 'A' = OK. STEP 4 GET /webapp/resdb.dotaz.proveddotazsql?PIDDOTAZ={token}&PPOZICE=0 → body contains 'OK'. STEP 5 (results + PAGINATION) GET /webapp/resdb.print_vysledek.Vysledek?pIdDotaz={token}&pLang=CS&pRadStart={row offset: 0,20,40,...} → HTML table, data rows = tr.trdata, per-row record id in input.hitlist[data-id]. STEP 6 (detail) POST /webapp/resdb.print_detail.Detail with pIdSpis={data-id}, pLang=CS, pIdDotaz={token}, pD={Date.now()}; timeline in div.casosaobal > div.tlpoint (span.dtm = date). STABLE STATELESS PERMALINKS (no dotaz needed): GET /webapp/resdb.print_detail.det?pspis=OZ/542865&plang=CS (also pspis=PT/1969-4629, PUV/25068 — {TYPE}/{number}). Other confirmed procedures: !resdb.oza.frm (TM search form), !resdb.pta.frm (patent form), !resdb.glob.frm (combined search), pts.det?xprim={id}&lan=cs (legacy detail), hxmptn?psymb=A01K (IPC codebook), epinfo.predpoklady. pD is only a cache-buster; the scraper author reported the chained flow is order-sensitive/fragile (identical results returned when the sequence was wrong).

ÚPV OPEN DATA — registers only, NOT the decisions database. Dataset landing pages (harvested into NKOD/data.gov.cz and data.europa.eu): GET /webapp/webapp.opendata.datovasada?ptyp={pt|tm|ud|pt96|tm96|ds96}&pid={YYYYMMDD}diff (daily increments) or pid={YYYYMMDD}full&ppart={N} (partitioned annual full exports) — verbatim examples: ptyp=ds96&pid=20260218diff; ptyp=tm96&pid=20260328diff; ptyp=pt96&pid=20250801full&ppart=167. Legacy HTML index with direct ZIP links: GET https://isdv.upv.cz/webapp/webapp.opendata.tm (anchor hrefs ending .zip; *_PIC.zip are image archives — the kokes/ngod downloader scrapes exactly this). CKAN-style catalog call seen: GET /webapp/webapp.opendata.package_show?id=ud. Another ZIP listing app: GET /webapp/webapp.pubsrv.seznam?pid=41. Content: WIPO ST.96 XML (schemas hosted at https://isdv.upv.gov.cz/doc/xsd/ST96/...). Documentation: https://isdv.upv.gov.cz/doc/opendata/doc/tm-dokumentace.html, .../ds-dokumentace.html, terms at .../podminky_uziti.html. The ÚPV open-data page additionally mentions a data service for the official notice board (úřední deska), a web service (API) for the legal status of a file (právní stav spisu), and an RSS feed — their endpoints could not be established from outside. NO dataset of správní/soudní rozhodnutí exists in the catalog — live HTML scraping is the only machine route to the decisions DB.

findings.caveats: (1) The target hosts (isdv.upv.gov.cz, isdv.upv.cz, upv.gov.cz) plus web.archive.org, Common Crawl, wipo.int, data.europa.eu and ikaros.cz were ALL egress-blocked in this environment, so no endpoint was executed live; everything comes from Google-indexed verbatim URLs, GitHub code, and search snippets. Endpoints seen verbatim (rozhodnuti.prochazet, dbr.rozhodnuti.Prochazet, rozhodnuti.SeznamRozhodnuti, rozhodnuti.showDocP?p_id=..., dbr.rozsudek.seznam, all resdb.* and webapp.opendata.* URLs) are high-confidence; the FORM FIELD NAMES / HTTP method of the decisions search ('Vyhledat') and the pagination parameters of SeznamRozhodnuti were NOT established — the first implementation step must be one live fetch of rozhodnuti.prochazet to read the form markup (expect a plain HTML form, possibly the resdb-style dotaz flow). (2) No documented public API for the search portal (independently confirmed by parkerhancock/patent-client-agents research notes); no open-data dump of decisions — scraping is the only route. (3) mod_plsql behavior: procedure names case-insensitive; unknown/misspelled parameter names typically return HTTP 404 'PROCEDURE ... NOT FOUND'-style errors — keep parameter names exact. (4) The chained resdb query flow is order-sensitive and was reported flaky by its author (same results regardless of criteria when the sequence broke); pD is just a Date.now() cache-buster. State lives server-side keyed by the iddotaz token in the URL, not in cookies — fine for serverless, but complete the whole chain within one request handler. (5) Many Google-indexed ISDV pages carry the title suffix 'Odstávka isdv.upv.cz' — the office runs maintenance windows and is phasing out the legacy isdv.upv.cz host; prefer isdv.upv.gov.cz and handle outage pages. (6) Politeness: the only known scraper used 10 s pauses; no rate-limit or WAF documentation found. Cookie-consent banner exists but content is served without cookies. (7) Decision texts are anonymized HTML; check response charset before decoding in Node (older ISDV pages historically used windows-1250 — unverified for current pages; read Content-Type and use TextDecoder accordingly). (8) showDocP p_id tokens are opaque 8-char ids; they are Google-indexed (so at least medium-term stable) but long-term permanence is unverified — always re-derive them from list pages rather than caching. (9) Licensing: open-data terms at /doc/opendata/doc/podminky_uziti.html cover only the register datasets; no explicit reuse license found for the decisions DB (public-sector information, decisions anonymized) — verify ToS/robots.txt before production scraping.

findings.source: EUIPO Guidelines for Examination (guidelines.euipo.europa.eu) — trademark, design and GI examination guidelines of the EU Intellectual Property Office

access.detail: PER-SECTION PAGES. URL scheme (verified verbatim from EUIPO's own OpenAPI specs, third-party code, and search-engine-indexed URLs): GET /{publicationId}/{topicId}/{publication-slug}/{topic-slug}. The two numeric IDs are canonical; both slugs are decorative and optional — GET /{publicationId}/{topicId} and even GET /{publicationId} (publication root / TOC) resolve. Examples seen verbatim: /2319054/2445755/trade-mark-guidelines/1-introduction (2026 EN TM edition, in force since 01/07/2026, Decision EX-26-09); /2302857/2231990/trade-mark-guidelines/1-introduction (2025 EN TM); /2214311/2046727/trade-mark-guidelines/11-2-substantive-requirements-for-priority-claims (2024 EN TM); /2058843/2047275/trade-mark-guidelines/11-priority (2023 EN TM); /2231430/2232593/designs-guidelines/7-authorisation and /2213908/2199801/designs-guidelines/1-introduction (designs); /1922895/1787768/trade-mark-guidelines/2-searches. LANGUAGES: each language+edition is a SEPARATE publicationId with its own topicIds and localized slugs — ES /2214313/2199807/directrices-sobre-marcas/1-introduccion, FR /2214315/2229982/directives-des-marques, EL /1778680/1698908/%CE%BA%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%B5%CF%85%CE%B8%CF%85%CE%BD%CF%84%CE%B7%CF%81%CE%B9%CE%B5%CF%82-... (percent-encoded Greek). 2025 edition exists in 23 EU languages; the in-force 2026 edition initially in the 5 working languages (EN/FR/DE/IT/ES). Old editions stay online at their IDs (stable permalinks per edition). PLATFORM (verified): the domain is a CNAME of euipo01app.sdlproducts.com (DNS resolved in-session: both → webapp-production-p394or-pres-1261056077.eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com, 34.253.180.166 / 54.76.150.207), i.e. an SDL/RWS-hosted LiveContent Reach-style delivery webapp publishing DITA content from EUIPO's Tridion Docs CMS; the mirror hostname serves identical URLs. RENDERING: could not be fetch-verified from this egress-blocked environment, but multiple lines of evidence say section text is present in the HTML and trivially extractable: thousands of deep pages across 23 languages are indexed with body-text snippets by Google/Bing/Firecrawl, and an independent research doc (patent-client author) concludes 'No documented public REST API... Trivial to scrape and chunk for retrieval' with 'HTML per chapter + downloadable PDF' and 'Auth: None'. For the MCP server: fetch the numeric URL with a browser-like User-Agent and Accept header, extract main content HTML→text; resolve CURRENT edition publicationIds at runtime by scraping the links on https://www.euipo.europa.eu/en/guidelines (also mirrored at https://eutm.euipo.europa.eu/en/guidelines) or the guidelines root page, since publicationIds change every annual edition.

PDF DOWNLOADS. GET /binary/{publicationId}/{binaryId} returns PDFs of the whole publication or of a Part/Section ('possibility to download a PDF on Part and Section level' — official EUIPO news). Verbatim examples from indexed URLs: /binary/2302857/2008000000 and /binary/2302857/2009000000 (2025 TM EN), /binary/2214311/2003000000, /binary/2058424/2000000000 (designs), /binary/1935305/2000220000 (ES), /binary/2058843/2007000000, /binary/2330038/2000000000 (GI craft/industrial guidelines, publication 2330038). BinaryIds follow a 20XX000000 series within each publication; there is no documented index of binaryIds — they are linked from the publication's pages. Whole-guidelines single-file PDFs also live on the main EUIPO site: https://euipo.europa.eu/tunnel-web/secure/webdav/guest/document_library/guidelines/trade_mark_guidelines_clean_en.pdf (clean version; track-changed variant also published per EUIPO, and per-language variants via the _en suffix), plus historical per-part PDFs under https://euipo.europa.eu/tunnel-web/secure/webdav/guest/document_library/contentPdfs/law_and_practice/... and .../contentPdfs/trade_marks/.... A platform tutorial PDF: https://euipo.europa.eu/tunnel-web/secure/webdav/guest/document_library/contentPdfs/law_and_practice/guidelines/guidelines_tutorial_en.pdf.

ON-SITE SEARCH — NOT ESTABLISHED. The site has a built-in 'advanced search' (scope: entire TM or Design publication, a specific Part, or a specific Section — official EUIPO news 'EUIPO Guidelines in electronic format: new functionalities'), but no search URL/endpoint is search-engine-indexed and no public code calls it; it is presumably an XHR against the SDL LiveContent Reach webapp (the underlying product exposes an internal search REST service — 'search.svc' pattern, JSESSIONID session cookie per RWS developer forum thread 'How to use the Search API in SDL LiveContent Reach?'), but the exact path/params on this host could not be verified from this egress-blocked environment. To pin it down: open any guidelines page with browser dev tools and capture the XHR fired by the search box. Serverless fallbacks that work today: (1) external search API scoped to site:guidelines.euipo.europa.eu, (2) fetch the publication root TOC and do your own matching over fetched sections. SEPARATE INTERNAL API (not public): EUIPO also runs Tridion Docs Dynamic Experience Delivery — dev instance seen verbatim in an EUIPO example repo: token endpoint https://dxd-live-euipo-development.tridion.sdlproducts.com/token.svc (OAuth2 client_credentials, client_id 'cduser') and GraphQL endpoint https://dxd-live-euipo-development.tridion.sdlproducts.com/cd/api with queries like publications(namespaceId:$namespaceId, first:$first){edges{node{id title}}}; this is a development host with credentials, not a public production API — do not build on it.

findings.caveats: All target domains (guidelines.euipo.europa.eu, euipo01app.sdlproducts.com, euipo.europa.eu, www.euipo.europa.eu, docs.rws.com, web.archive.org, commoncrawl) were egress-blocked in this environment, so NOTHING was verified by a live HTTP response; URL patterns are verbatim from EUIPO's own OpenAPI specs (which cite guidelines URLs), search-engine-indexed URLs on the official hosts, and third-party research/code. Specifically NOT established: (1) the on-site search endpoint; (2) whether section HTML is fully server-rendered (strong indirect evidence yes — heavy multilingual indexing plus an independent assessment 'trivial to scrape'; still, test with a plain Node fetch before committing, and send a browser-like User-Agent since the app sits behind an SDL-hosted AWS ELB that may filter default UAs); (3) sitemap.xml/robots.txt existence; (4) the HTML's content-container selectors; (5) an enumerable index of /binary/{pub}/{binary} PDF IDs. Structural caveats: publicationIds and topicIds change with every annual edition and differ per language — hardcoding IDs will silently pin you to an old edition; resolve current-edition IDs at runtime from https://www.euipo.europa.eu/en/guidelines (or the guidelines root) and treat numeric ID pairs as the stable per-edition permalink. The currently in-force 2026 edition (from 01/07/2026) exists only in EN/FR/DE/IT/ES; the 23-language coverage applies to the 2025 edition. No published rate limits; be polite (low concurrency, caching) — it is a hosted vendor app, not EUIPO-run infrastructure. Reuse: EUIPO content-reuse terms permit reuse of Office texts (check current EUIPO legal notice for attribution requirements). No GitHub scraper for the guidelines exists to copy from — the 20 total code hits for the domain are all mere citations.
